newsitem.title: UK: Protestant militant shot in N.Irish attack.
newsitem.headline: Protestant militant shot in N.Irish attack.

text.p: A Protestant militant was shot dead in north Belfast early on Tuesday, apparently victim of the undercurrent of lawlessness that has troubled Northern Ireland since rival guerrilla ceasefires two years ago.

Police said the Irish Republican Army (IRA), which is fighting to end British rule of Northern Ireland, was not responsible and sources linked to rival Protestant gunmen insisted that they were not to blame either.
The victim, Thomas Stewart, was suspended last week as a "commander" in a North Belfast branch of the Ulster Volunteer Force (UVF), an outlawed pro-British Protestant militia.

The reason for his suspension was not known. If he was killed by the UVF, this would be in breach of its two-year-old ceasefire and have repercussions for its political representatives at Belfast peace talks.

Police said Stewart, who was shot while walking along a north Belfast street, was most probably a victim of a crime wave including drug trafficking that has plagued many Protestant and Catholic neighbourhoods for much of the past two years.
Security sources said Protestant guerrillas had culled rich pickings from robberies, drugs and other crime, angering their commanders intent on maintaining discipline,

Protestant "brigadiers" who directed a wave of killings against Catholic nationalists before the ceasefire have held the line against internal pressure to retaliate for IRA violence and have cracked down on dissidents.
David Ervine, who leads a new political party which is close to the Protestant militia, blamed "criminal elements" for Stewart's killing.
"It is another tragedy, a sad and unnecessary death on the path of pain that is Ulster (Northern Ireland)," he said.
The IRA ended its ceasefire in February with a renewed war on British targets including an attack on its Northern Ireland army base this month, its first in the province for two years.
Security sources believe it is also responsible for killing of eight Catholics who were shot by gunmen styling themselves anti-drugs vigilantes over the past 18 months.
The IRA has never admitted the killings but most people on the streets of Catholic enclaves think that the vigilante group, Direct Action Against Drugs, is merely an IRA cover.
Both sets of guerrillas have exacted a violence price on individuals who fall foul of a law-and-order code in their own communities.

Since the ceasefires were declared in late 1994, several hundred people have been beaten by gangs wielding clubs, nail-studded baseball bats and hammers. Concrete blocks have been used to break their limbs.
